Autumn festival }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[Toyonaka]], [[Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{draft categories| }} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Toyonaka]] [[Category:History of Toyonaka]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Mukuhashi Sōja]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Mukuhashi Sōja]] [[en:Mukuhashi Sōja]] [[ja:%E6%A4%8B%E6%A9%8B%E7%B7%8F%E7%A4%BE]] [[sn:ukuhashi Sōja]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Mukuhashi Sōja}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}}

Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[Emperor Go-Toba]]. Autumn festival }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] }} [[sn:Mukuhashi Sōja]] [[ja:%E6%A4%8B%E6%A9%8B%E7%B7%8F%E7%A4%BE]] [[sn:ukuhashi Sōja]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[ja:椋橋総社]]

Autumn festival }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[:en:Shōnai Station (Osaka)|Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] }} [[sn:Mukuhashi Sōja]] [[sn:E6%A4%8B%E6%A9%8B%E7%B7%8F%E7%A4%BE]] [[sn:ukuhashi Sōja]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[ja:椋橋総社]] [[Category:paes with no wikidata]]

Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[:en:Shōnai Station (Osaka)|Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] }} [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[ja:椋橋総社]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}}

Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|qid=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[:en:Shōnai Station (Osaka)|Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] }} [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}}

[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] | sacred_objects = | shrine_Rank = | founding_date = Unknown | priest = | main_hall = | alternative_names = Koi no Miya (Shrine of the Carp) | pilgrimages = | annual_festival = October 14 | rituals = [[Tōka Ebisu]]
Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[:en:Shōnai Station (Osaka)|Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] }} [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] | sacred_objects = | shrine_Rank = | founding_date = Unknown | priest = | main_hall = | alternative_names = Koi no Miya (Shrine of the Carp) | pilgrimages = | annual_festival = October 14 | rituals = [[Tōka Ebisu]]
Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[Shōmotomachi]], [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest [[:en:Toyonaka|Toyonaka]] and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]]). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]], who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to [[:en:Silla|Silla]].''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by [[:en:Oda Nobunaga|Oda Nobunaga]]. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk [[:en:Gyōki|Gyōki]], who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of [[:en:Emperor Go-Toba|Emperor Go-Toba]]. Disputes over the manor's land with the [[:en:Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura shogunate]] contributed to the outbreak of the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to [[:en:Sugawara no Michizane|Sugawara no Michizane]], originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from [[:en:Kanzakigawa Station|Kanzakigawa Station]]. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from [[:en:Shōnai Station (Osaka)|Shōnai Station (Osaka)]]. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Shōmotomachi]], {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka}} and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|WD=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla}}.''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|WD=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|WD=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}}, who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|en|Emperor Go-Toba|WD=Q316658|lt=Emperor Go-Toba}}. the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from {{ill|Kanzakigawa Station|en|Kanzakigawa Station|WD=Q3969851|lt=Kanzakigawa Station}}. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from {{ill|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|en|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|WD=Q7506184|lt=Shōnai Station (Osaka)}}. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Autumn festival | location = {{ill|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.74341666666667|N|135.46066666666667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} [[File:境外鳥居.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Kurahashi Sōsha''' (椋橋総社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Shōmotomachi]], {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|WD=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka}} and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|WD=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla}}.''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|WD=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|WD=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}}, who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|en|Emperor Go-Toba|WD=Q316658|lt=Emperor Go-Toba}}. the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from {{ill|Kanzakigawa Station|en|Kanzakigawa Station|WD=Q3969851|lt=Kanzakigawa Station}}. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from {{ill|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|en|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|WD=Q7506184|lt=Shōnai Station (Osaka)}}. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyonaka]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:pages]]

Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|WD=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka|1=Toyonaka}} and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|WD=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture|1=Hyōgo Prefecture}}). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}}, in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}}, who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}}.''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.'' In the 16th century, the shrine became a favored site for the military elite, including contributions from [[Fujihara Hideyasu]] in 1391 and [[Ikeda Chikugo no Kami]] during the [[Tenshō period]]. However, much of the shrine was destroyed during the [[Siege of Arioka Castle]] in 1579, initiated by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|WD=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga|1=Oda Nobunaga}}. The current shrine structures date to 1917, rebuilt after a fire caused by the collapse of a lantern in 1916. === Carp Legend === A prominent legend recounts that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] arrived in the region riding a carp. Another tale involves the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|WD=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki|1=Gyōki}}, who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|en|Emperor Go-Toba|WD=Q316658|lt=Emperor Go-Toba|1=Emperor Go-Toba}}. Another tale involves the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|WD=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki|1=Gyōki}}, who prayed for divine intervention to construct a bridge over the fast currents of the Ina River. Carp gathered to form a "bridge," enabling the construction to succeed. Villagers revered the carp as messengers of the gods, abstaining from consuming them and releasing any caught into the shrine's sacred carp pond. === Cultural Heritage === The shrine was previously called Gozu Tennō Shrine and was known as one of the "Three Great Gozu Tennō Shrines of Toyoshima District" alongside [[Yasaka Shrine (Ikeda City)|Kanda Yasaka Shrine]] and [[Togura Kasuga Shrine]]. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, Kurahashi Manor was the territory of [[Kamegiku]] (later [[Iga no Tsubone]]), a favorite consort of {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|en|Emperor Go-Toba|WD=Q316658|lt=Emperor Go-Toba|1=Emperor Go-Toba}}. Disputes over the manor's land with the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|WD=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate|1=Kamakura shogunate}} contributed to the outbreak of the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221. == Worshipped Deities == * Main deities: ''' [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] (Gozu Tennō) ''' {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}} == Shrine Grounds == * '''Main hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Worship hall''' - Rebuilt in 1917. * '''Shusse Kamegiku Tenmangū''' - Dedicated to {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|en|Sugawara no Michizane|WD=Q382005|lt=Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane}}, originally established for the faith of [[Kamegiku]]. * '''Ebisu Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Sansha Shrine''' - Enshrines [[Sumiyoshi Ōkami]], [[Kasuga Ōkami]], and [[Atago Gongen]]. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Dedicated to [[Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto]]. * '''Koi-zuka''' - A Kofun for deceased sacred carp. * '''Sacred tree''' - A fusion of a camphor tree and glossy privet, symbolizing harmony and good relationships. * '''Koi pond''' * '''Shōmoto Kindergarten''' - Adjacent to the shrine. === Outer Structures === * '''Torii''' - Located 200 meters south of the shrine; the current torii was rebuilt in 1996 following the [[1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake]]. * '''Kurahashi Shrine Otabisho''' - A temporary resting place for divine spirits during processions, located 500 meters south of the shrine. == festivals == * New Year festival: January 1 * Ebisu festival: January 9–11 * Spring festival: April 14 * Summer festival: July 14 * '''Autumn Grand festival''': October 13–14 ''' Features traditional ''futon taiko'' (portable drum floats). == Access == * [[:en:Hankyu Kobe Line|Hankyu Kobe Line]]: 22-minute walk northwest from {{ill|Kanzakigawa Station|en|Kanzakigawa Station|WD=Q3969851|lt=Kanzakigawa Station|1=Kanzakigawa Station}}. * [[:en:Hankyu Takarazuka Line|Hankyu Takarazuka Line]]: 28-minute walk southwest from {{ill|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|en|Shōnai Station (Osaka)|WD=Q7506184|lt=Shōnai Station (Osaka)|1=Shōnai Station (Osaka)}}. * [[Hankyu Bus]]: 4-minute walk from "Shōmoto" stop. * [[Hanshin Bus]]: 11-minute walk from "Tonoichi 2-chome" stop. == See Also == * [[Shōnai, Toyonaka|Shōnai]] * [[Kurahashi Manor]] * [[Kurahashi Castle]] * [[Toyoshima District]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai1sibu/toyonaka-city/m04.html Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] * [http://www.city.toyonaka.osaka.jp/toyonaka//kankyo/kankyo/hyakkei/a_south/s_01.html Toyonaka Scenic Spots] {{shinto-stub}} {{pref-stub-Osaka Prefecture}} {{Japan-hist-stub}} {{Hachiman Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|椋橋総社|version=104216695|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:椋橋総社]] {{wikidata link|Q54153289}} [[Category:Buildings and structures in Toyonaka]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Regional Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Known for its ancient carp legend, it is also referred to as the "Shrine of the Carp" (鯉の宮). == History == === Origin === The shrine has long been regarded as the main tutelary shrine of the Kurahashi Manor (椋橋荘), an estate established in the mid-12th century under the [[Sekkan family]]'s rule. The manor was divided into East Kurahashi Manor and West Kurahashi Manor, located at the confluence of the [[:en:Ina River|Ina River]] and [[Kanzaki River]] (present-day southwest {{ill|Toyonaka|en|Toyonaka|qid=Q467479|lt=Toyonaka|1=Toyonaka}} and [[Tonoichi, Amagasaki|Tonoichi, Amagasaki]] in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture|1=Hyōgo Prefecture}}). Tradition holds that in ancient times, [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] descended to the area riding on a carp via the river. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}}, in November of the 7th year of his reign (91 BCE), the ancestor of the Kurahashi Clan, [[Ikagashikoo no Mikoto]], established the shrine.Kurahashi Sōsha, ''History of Kurahashi Sōsha.''Toji ancient documents, ''Shinsen Shōjiroku.'' === Historical Significance === Kurahashi Manor, well-documented in historical records, was home to the Kurahashi Muraji clan and its vassals. It consisted of 24 villages: 14 in East Kurahashi Manor and 10 in West Kurahashi Manor. The shrine also holds a connection to {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}}, who is said to have prayed for blessings here before her expedition to {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}}.''Settsu Fudoki,'' ''Nango Kasuga Old Records,'' ''Toyoshima District History.''
